subject: botany_2
question_text: What are the differences between DNA and RNA?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.34, printed question 42. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK NOTE: the guide's row 7 reads "DNA is genetic material / RNA is non-genetic material". As a general claim that is false, and this same book contradicts it — its own SAQ 27 and VSAQ 95 say TMV, polio virus and HIV carry RNA as their genetic material. The card qualifies the row: in cellular organisms DNA is the genetic material, but in many viruses RNA is.

insider_note: Ten rows in the book, four marks on the paper. Tabulate — two columns, numbered rows — and get at least eight differences down.

steps.label: Name, strands and sugar
steps.margin_note: Set up two columns on the first line. Four numbered rows here.
lines: 3. Sugar is DEOXYRIBOSE  | Sugar is RIBOSE
4. Bases A, T, G, C      | Bases A, U, G, C
steps.why: The one missing oxygen in deoxyribose is what makes DNA the more stable molecule, so the sugar row explains the stability row that follows.
common_mistakes: Saying RNA has thymine. RNA has URACIL in place of thymine.
Saying DNA is single stranded. DNA is DOUBLE stranded.
steps.memory_tip: Deoxy means one oxygen less, and that is what makes it stable.

steps.label: Stability and size
steps.margin_note: Three more numbered rows. The alkali row is the one examiners like.
steps.why: The extra hydroxyl group on ribose is what makes RNA break down in alkali, so its instability follows directly from its sugar.
common_mistakes: Saying RNA is more stable. DNA is the stable one.
Giving no size figures. The nucleotide counts are worth writing.
steps.memory_tip: One extra oxygen makes RNA easier to break.

steps.label: Replication and function
steps.margin_note: Three more rows. Keep the columns aligned.
lines: 9. Does NOT take part directly in protein
synthesis | Takes part DIRECTLY in protein
steps.why: DNA stays in the nucleus as the archive and RNA does the work outside it, which is why only one of them replicates.
common_mistakes: Saying DNA makes protein directly. It does NOT; RNA does.
Saying RNA replicates. In cells it does not — it is transcribed from DNA.
steps.memory_tip: DNA is the master copy; RNA is the working copy.

steps.label: Types and base pairing
steps.margin_note: The three RNA types, both base-pairing rules, and the qualified genetic-material row.
lines: 12. Base pairing A = T and G ≡ C
| Base pairing A = U and G ≡ C
13. In CELLS, DNA is the genetic material.
In many VIRUSES — TMV, polio, HIV — RNA is
steps.why: Saying RNA is 'non-genetic' would contradict the virus chapter of this same syllabus, so the claim has to be limited to cellular organisms.
common_mistakes: Writing that RNA is never genetic material. TMV, polio and HIV all use RNA. The guide prints the unqualified claim.
Naming two types of RNA. There are THREE: mRNA, tRNA and rRNA.
steps.memory_tip: RNA is genetic material too, just not in cells.
